text:
jean: heads up — while ramping the canary sampling for the new routing policy i saw raw user payloads in console inspect for a chat route. looks like PII surfaced for ~6 requests. need quick mitigation.

sam: which route + tenant? any screenshots?

jean: /v1/chat/streaming, tenant=internal-alpha. attaching console snippet (copied): shows unredacted user.email and phone in body. sampling = 1% transient for this canary.

mira: is this coming from inspect-mode or the real sampler? if inspect-mode was enabled it can bypass some redaction paths.

alan: sounds like sampler is running before the scrubber. sam — can you paste the sampler/redact order from the canary config?

sam: sure — config snip:```json
{"pipeline": ["sampler", "enricher", "router", "scrubber", "inspector"]}
```

alan: yep — sampler before scrubber. that's the issue. we should never let raw payloads reach inspector unless route is allowlisted/approved.

mira: options: 1) move sampler after scrubber so any sampled payloads are already redacted, 2) keep sampler early but run a minimal pre-scrub (cheap heuristics) that masks obvious emails/phones before sampling. 1 is safest but will cost more CPU since we redact every request.

jean: quick mitigation we can flip: console.inspect should not show request bodies for non-allowlisted routes. that buys time.

ops-bot: Toggle applied — @sarah set console.inspect=false for group:internal-alpha at 2026-03-20T15:42:07Z

sarah: applied. also propose adding a "pre_scrub: fast_mask" boolean to pipeline to run cheap regex masks before sampler. will catch most emails/phones/nat ids.

mira: regex masks are best short-term fix. longer term we need a real pre-scrub heuristics (token-level NER) but that’s heavier. i'll add a metric: telemetry.pre_scrub_fallback_rate so we can see how often fast_mask fails and full-redact triggers.

jean: also want a safe_inspect flag per-route: if true, inspector will only show sampled payloads after full-redaction regardless of sampler position. otherwise inspector must never show raw.

sam: proposed config change:```yaml
route_config:
  pre_scrub: fast_mask  # quick regex masks before sampler
  safe_inspect: true    # ensures inspector sees redacted payloads
  sampler_order: keep_early # default but can be post_redact for high-risk routes
```

alan: rollout/UX note — console toggle needs clearer affordance: show which routes are in "safe_inspect" mode and which are temporarily suppressed. people re-enable inspect without realizing. add tooltip + banner.

mira: agree. dashboard tiles: show inspect-enabled routes, sampled_count, unredacted_count (should be zero) and pre_scrub_fallback_rate. if unredacted_count > 0 alert oncall.

sam: i'll open the PR tonight targeting a small canary that flips pipeline to include pre_scrub. plan: canary -> monitor unredacted_count and latency delta. oncall: alert if unredacted_count > 0 after 10m.

jean: :thumbsup: thanks. quick legal FYI — they want interim notice. do we need an SLA change or just flagged incident?

sarah: legal looped in. added temporary audit retention + evidence log for the 6 affected traces; posted details in #security.

jean: action items: sam opens PR (pre_scrub + safe_inspect), mira adds telemetry tiles and alert, alan updates console UX copy, sarah confirms legal ack. reconvene after canary metrics.

sam: on it. will ping when PR is up.

mira: adding dashboard widgets now. will share chronicle in ~2hrs. :eyes:

alan: small add — make default sampler decisions derived from metadata only (route, tenant, response_code) so we reduce need to look at body before scrubbing. that helps long term.

jean: agreed. thank you everyone. keep oncall posted.
